fr.B: Dans tout le pays d’Égypte, la grêle frappa tout ce qui se trouvait dans les champs, gens et bêtes. Elle coucha toutes les plantes des champs et fracassa tous les arbres.
fr.R: La grêle a frappé tout ce qui était dans les champs, dans toute l’Égypte. Elle a frappé les gens et les animaux. Elle a couché toutes les plantes et cassé tous les arbres.

sw.L: Na mvua ya mawe ikapiga, katika nchi yote ya Misri, vyote vilivyokuwa kondeni, tangu mwanadamu hadi mnyama; na mvua ya mawe ikapiga kila mmea wa kondeni, nayo ikavunjavunja kila mti wa kondeni.
sw.B: Katika nchi yote ya Misri, mvua ya mawe ilipiga kila kitu kilichokuwa mashambani, watu na wanyama. Ikaangusha mimea yote ya mashambani na kuipasua miti yote.
sw.R: Mvua ya mawe ilipiga kila kitu kilichokuwa mashambani katika Misri yote. Iliwapiga watu na wanyama. Ikaangusha mimea yote na kuvunja miti yote.

decisions.choice: from man to beast: people and animals alike
decisions.reason: The phrase names both ends of a range and means everything in between.

decisions.choice: shattered: broke in pieces
decisions.reason: The verb is the stronger form of "break": the trees were smashed.

source.text: רַ֚ק בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֔שֶׁן אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹ֥א הָיָ֖ה בָּרָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Only in [the] land of Goshen, where there [were the] sons of Israel, not was hail.

en.L: Only in the land of Goshen, where the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel [were], there was no hail.
en.B: Only in the land of Goshen, where the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} lived, was there no hail.
en.R: But no hail fell in Goshen, where the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} lived.

es.L: Solo en la tierra de Gosén, donde [estaban] los hijos de Israel, no hubo granizo.
es.B: Solamente en la región de Gosén, donde vivían los israelitas, no cayó granizo.
es.R: Pero en Gosén, donde vivían los israelitas, no cayó granizo.

fr.L: Seulement dans le pays de Goshen, où [étaient] les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, il n’y eut pas de grêle.
fr.B: Seule la région de Goshen, où vivaient les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, fut épargnée par la grêle.
fr.R: Mais la grêle n’est pas tombée dans la région de Goshen, où vivaient les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}.

sw.L: Ila katika nchi ya Gosheni, walikokuwa wana wa Israeli, haikuwa mvua ya mawe.
sw.B: Ni katika nchi ya Gosheni tu, walimoishi Waisraeli, ambamo mvua ya mawe haikunyesha.
sw.R: Lakini mvua ya mawe haikunyesha Gosheni, walikoishi Waisraeli.

decisions.choice: only in Goshen: the distinction again
decisions.reason: As with the flies (8:18) and the livestock (verses 4, 6), God spares the place where Israel lives. It happens again with the darkness (10:23).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח פַּרְעֹ֗ה וַיִּקְרָא֙ לְמֹשֶׁ֣ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֖ם חָטָ֣אתִי הַפָּ֑עַם יְהוָה֙ הַצַּדִּ֔יק וַאֲנִ֥י וְעַמִּ֖י הָרְשָׁעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Pharaoh and summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them, I have sinned this time; Yahweh [is] the righteous [one], and I and my people [are] the wicked [ones].

en.L: And Pharaoh sent and called Moses and Aaron and said to them, "I have sinned this time; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] the righteous one, and I and my people [are] the wicked ones.
en.B: Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said to them, "I have sinned this time. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is in the right, and the guilt lies with me and my people.
en.R: Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron. He said to them, "I have sinned this time. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has done what is right. My people and I are the ones who have done wrong.

es.L: Y envió el faraón y llamó a Moisés y a Aarón, y les dijo: «He pecado esta vez; {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [es] el justo, y yo y mi pueblo [somos] los malvados.
es.B: El faraón mandó llamar a Moisés y a Aarón y les dijo: «Esta vez he pecado. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tiene la razón, y la culpa es mía y de mi pueblo.
es.R: El faraón mandó llamar a Moisés y a Aarón. Les dijo: «Esta vez he pecado. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha actuado con justicia. Mi pueblo y yo somos los que hemos hecho el mal.

fr.L: Et Pharaon envoya appeler Moïse et Aaron, et leur dit : « J’ai péché cette fois ; {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] le juste, et moi et mon peuple [sommes] les méchants.
fr.B: Pharaon fit appeler Moïse et Aaron et leur dit : « Cette fois, j’ai péché. C’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui a raison, et la faute est à moi et à mon peuple.
fr.R: Pharaon a fait appeler Moïse et Aaron. Il leur a dit : « Cette fois, j’ai péché. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a agi avec justice. C’est mon peuple et moi qui avons mal agi.

sw.L: Naye Farao akatuma, akawaita Musa na Haruni, akawaambia, "Nimetenda dhambi safari hii; {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ndiye] mwenye haki, nami na watu wangu [ndio] waovu.
sw.B: Farao aliwaita Musa na Haruni, akawaambia, "Safari hii nimetenda dhambi. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yuko sahihi, na hatia ni yangu na ya watu wangu.
sw.R: Farao aliwaita Musa na Haruni. Akawaambia, "Safari hii nimetenda dhambi. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametenda haki. Mimi na watu wangu ndio tuliokosea.

decisions.choice: righteous ... wicked: in the right ... in the wrong
decisions.reason: The two words are the terms of a court case: the righteous party is the one in the right, the wicked party the one found guilty (Deuteronomy 25:1). Pharaoh admits that in this dispute Yahweh is in the right and he and his people are at fault. He does not necessarily confess faith in Yahweh.

decisions.choice: this time: on this occasion
decisions.reason: Pharaoh admits fault for now. The phrase may limit the confession to this one instance, and verse 34 shows it did not last.

decisions.choice: in the right ... the guilt lies with / has done what is right ... have done wrong
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "righteous" and "wicked". Balanced and Readable use the language of a court case to show the sense; "righteous" here is not the Greek key term.

source.text: הַעְתִּ֨ירוּ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְרַ֕ב מִֽהְיֹ֛ת קֹלֹ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים וּבָרָ֑ד וַאֲשַׁלְּחָ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תֹסִפ֖וּן לַעֲמֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Entreat Yahweh, and [there is] enough of being thunders of God and hail; and I will let go you, and not you will continue to stay.

en.L: Entreat {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for [there has been] enough of the thunder of God and hail. And I will let you go, and you will not stay any longer."
en.B: Plead with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. There has been enough of God's thunder and hail. I will release you. You will stay here no longer."
en.R: Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! We cannot take any more of God's thunder and hail. I will let you go. You can leave right away."

es.L: {{plural_you:Rueguen|Rogad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque [ya ha habido] bastante de truenos de Dios y granizo. Y yo {{plural_you:los|os}} dejaré ir, y no {{plural_you:se quedarán|os quedaréis}} más».
es.B: {{plural_you:Supliquen|Suplicad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Ya ha habido bastantes truenos de Dios y granizo. Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} dejaré salir. No {{plural_you:se quedarán|os quedaréis}} aquí más tiempo».
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Oren|Orad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}! Ya no aguantamos más los truenos de Dios y el granizo. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} dejaré ir. {{plural_you:Pueden irse|Podéis iros}} ahora mismo».

fr.L: Suppliez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, car [il y a eu] assez de tonnerres de Dieu et de grêle. Et je vous laisserai aller, et vous ne resterez pas davantage. »
fr.B: Intercédez auprès {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Il y a eu assez de tonnerres de Dieu et de grêle. Je vais vous laisser partir ; vous ne resterez pas ici plus longtemps. »
fr.R: Priez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Nous n’en pouvons plus des tonnerres de Dieu et de la grêle. Je vais vous laisser partir. Vous pouvez vous en aller tout de suite. »

sw.L: Mwombeni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana zimetosha ngurumo za Mungu na mvua ya mawe. Nami nitawaacha mwende, wala hamtaendelea kukaa."
sw.B: Mwombeni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ngurumo za Mungu na mvua ya mawe zimetosha. Nitawaachilia; hamtakaa hapa tena."
sw.R: Mwombeni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Hatuwezi kuvumilia tena ngurumo za Mungu na mvua ya mawe. Nitawaacha mwende. Mnaweza kuondoka mara moja."

decisions.choice: thunder of God: thunder sent by God, or mighty thunder
decisions.reason: Pharaoh most likely means the thunder God is sending. The word for God can also be used to mean "mighty" or "tremendous" (compare "a great city to God" in Jonah 3:3), so the phrase may mean "tremendous thunder".

decisions.choice: entreat: pray on someone's behalf
decisions.reason: The verb of 8:4, 24. Pharaoh asks for prayer a third time.

decisions.choice: you will not continue to stay: you will stay no longer
decisions.reason: Pharaoh promises immediate release, without the limits he set in 8:21, 24.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כְּצֵאתִי֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר אֶפְרֹ֥שׂ אֶת־כַּפַּ֖י אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה הַקֹּל֣וֹת יֶחְדָּל֗וּן וְהַבָּרָד֙ לֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶה־ע֔וֹד לְמַ֣עַן תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֥י לַיהוָ֖ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Moses, as I go out [of] the city I will spread out my palms to Yahweh; the thunders will cease, and the hail will not be again, so that you may know that to Yahweh [belongs] the earth.

en.L: And Moses said to him, "When I go out of the city, I will spread out my palms to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The thunder will cease, and there will be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth [belongs] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Moses replied, "As soon as I am outside the city, I will spread my hands out toward {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the thunder will end and the hail will be gone, and you will learn that the earth belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Moses said to Pharaoh, "When I go outside the city, I will raise my hands and pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The thunder and hail will end. Then you will know that the earth belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y le dijo Moisés: «Cuando yo salga de la ciudad, extenderé mis palmas {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Los truenos cesarán, y no habrá más granizo, para que sepas que {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} [es] la tierra.
es.B: Moisés respondió: «En cuanto haya salido de la ciudad, extenderé las manos hacia {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Entonces cesarán los truenos y ya no habrá granizo, y sabrás que la tierra pertenece {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Moisés le dijo al faraón: «Cuando salga de la ciudad, levantaré las manos y oraré {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Los truenos y el granizo se acabarán. Así sabrás que la tierra es {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et Moïse lui dit : « Quand je sortirai de la ville, j’étendrai mes paumes vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Les tonnerres cesseront, et il n’y aura plus de grêle, afin que tu saches que la terre [est] {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Moïse répondit : « Dès que je serai sorti de la ville, je tendrai les mains vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Alors le tonnerre cessera et il n’y aura plus de grêle, et tu sauras que la terre appartient {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Moïse a dit à Pharaon : « Quand je serai sorti de la ville, je lèverai les mains pour prier {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Le tonnerre et la grêle s’arrêteront. Alors tu sauras que la terre appartient {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Naye Musa akamwambia, "Nitakapotoka mjini, nitavikunjua viganja vyangu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ngurumo zitakoma, wala hakutakuwa tena na mvua ya mawe, ili ujue kwamba dunia [ni] ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Musa alijibu, "Mara nitakapokuwa nje ya mji, nitanyoosha mikono yangu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ndipo ngurumo zitakoma na mvua ya mawe itakwisha, nawe utajua kwamba dunia ni mali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Musa alimwambia Farao, "Nikitoka nje ya mji, nitainua mikono yangu na kumwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ngurumo na mvua ya mawe vitakoma. Ndipo utajua kwamba dunia ni ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: spread out my palms: the posture of prayer
decisions.reason: Praying with open hands spread toward heaven is described in 1 Kings 8:22, 38 and Isaiah 1:15. The text does not say why Moses prays outside the city.

decisions.choice: the earth belongs to Yahweh: he rules the whole earth, not only Israel
decisions.reason: The same claim is made in 19:5 and Psalm 24:1. The word can also mean "the land", Egypt itself, but here it most likely means the whole earth, as in verses 14 and 16.

decisions.choice: raise my hands and pray
decisions.reason: Readable says that the gesture is prayer.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֖ה וַעֲבָדֶ֑יךָ יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֚י טֶ֣רֶם תִּֽירְא֔וּן מִפְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And you and your servants, I know that not yet you fear before Yahweh God.

en.L: But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God."
en.B: But you and your officials, I know, have yet to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God."
en.R: But I know this about you and your officials: you still do not fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God."

es.L: Pero en cuanto a ti y a tus siervos, sé que todavía no {{plural_you:temen|teméis}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} Dios».
es.B: Pero sé que tú y tus funcionarios todavía no {{plural_you:temen|teméis}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} Dios».
es.R: Pero esto sé de ti y de tus funcionarios: todavía no {{plural_you:temen|teméis}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} Dios».

fr.L: Mais quant à toi et à tes serviteurs, je sais que vous ne craignez pas encore {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu. »
fr.B: Mais toi et tes officiers, je le sais, vous ne craignez pas encore {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu. »
fr.R: Mais je sais une chose sur toi et sur tes officiers : vous ne craignez toujours pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu. »

sw.L: Lakini wewe na watumishi wako, najua kwamba bado hamjamcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu."
sw.B: Lakini wewe na maafisa wako, najua, bado hamjamcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu."
sw.R: Lakini ninajua hili kuhusu wewe na maafisa wako: bado hammchi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu."

decisions.choice: Yahweh God: the divine name joined with the word for God
decisions.reason: The pairing is used throughout Genesis 2:4-3:24 but is rare elsewhere in the Pentateuch. Here it may stress that Yahweh, whom Pharaoh has just named (verse 27), is God.

decisions.choice: not yet fear: Pharaoh fears the storm, not Yahweh
decisions.reason: Fear of Yahweh means reverence that obeys (verse 20). Pharaoh has confessed, but Moses knows the confession will not last (verse 34).

decisions.choice: your officials
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are his court and officials (5:21; 8:5). Balanced and Readable say "officials"; Literal keeps "servants".

source.text: וְהַפִּשְׁתָּ֥ה וְהַשְּׂעֹרָ֖ה נֻכָּ֑תָה כִּ֤י הַשְּׂעֹרָה֙ אָבִ֔יב וְהַפִּשְׁתָּ֖ה גִּבְעֹֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley [was in the] ear and the flax [in] bud.

en.L: And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley [was] in the ear, and the flax [was] in bud.
en.B: The flax and barley crops were lost, because the barley had already headed out and the flax had come into flower.
en.R: The hail destroyed the flax, a plant used to make linen cloth, and the barley. The barley plants already had grain on them, and the flax plants had flowers.

es.L: Y el lino y la cebada fueron heridos, porque la cebada [estaba] en espiga y el lino [estaba] en flor.
es.B: Se perdieron las cosechas de lino y de cebada, porque la cebada ya estaba espigada y el lino había florecido.
es.R: El granizo destruyó el lino, una planta con la que se hace la tela de lino, y también la cebada. Las plantas de cebada ya tenían grano, y las de lino tenían flores.

fr.L: Et le lin et l’orge furent frappés, car l’orge [était] en épis et le lin [était] en boutons.
fr.B: Le lin et l’orge furent perdus, car l’orge avait déjà ses épis et le lin était en fleur.
fr.R: La grêle a détruit le lin, une plante qui sert à faire de la toile, et l’orge. Les épis d’orge étaient déjà sortis, et le lin avait des fleurs.

sw.L: Na kitani na shayiri vikapigwa, kwa maana shayiri [ilikuwa] imetoa masuke na kitani [kilikuwa] kimechanua.
sw.B: Mazao ya kitani na shayiri yaliharibika, kwa sababu shayiri ilikuwa imekwisha kutoa masuke na kitani kilikuwa kimechanua maua.
sw.R: Mvua ya mawe iliharibu kitani, mmea unaotumiwa kutengeneza nguo za kitani, pamoja na shayiri. Mimea ya shayiri ilikuwa tayari na nafaka, na mimea ya kitani ilikuwa na maua.

decisions.choice: barley in the ear, flax in bud: the time of year
decisions.reason: Verses 31-32 are a note from the narrator. Barley and flax grow faster than wheat and spelt; when barley is in the ear the other grains are still young. The word for the barley's ear gives its name to Abib, the month of the exodus (13:4; 23:15). The hail fell some weeks before that spring month.

decisions.choice: in bud: in flower, forming seed heads
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It may mean that the flax was in bloom or that its seed heads were forming.

decisions.choice: a plant used to make linen cloth
decisions.reason: Readable says what flax is.

decisions.choice: The hail
decisions.reason: Readable names what struck the crops, from verse 25.

source.text: וְהַחִטָּ֥ה וְהַכֻּסֶּ֖מֶת לֹ֣א נֻכּ֑וּ כִּ֥י אֲפִילֹ֖ת הֵֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the wheat and the spelt not were struck, for late [are] they.

en.L: But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they [are] late.
en.B: The wheat and spelt escaped, since they are later crops.
en.R: But the wheat was not hurt. Neither was another kind of wheat called spelt. They come up later in the year.

es.L: Pero el trigo y la espelta no fueron heridos, porque [son] tardíos.
es.B: El trigo y la espelta se salvaron, porque son cultivos más tardíos.
es.R: Pero al trigo no le pasó nada. Tampoco a otra clase de trigo llamada espelta. Estos crecen más tarde en el año.

fr.L: Mais le blé et l’épeautre ne furent pas frappés, car ils [sont] tardifs.
fr.B: Le blé et l’épeautre furent épargnés, parce que ce sont des cultures plus tardives.
fr.R: Mais le blé n’a pas été abîmé. Une autre sorte de blé, l’épeautre, non plus. Ils poussent plus tard dans l’année.

sw.L: Lakini ngano na spelti havikupigwa, kwa maana [ni] vya kuchelewa.
sw.B: Ngano na spelti viliponea, kwa kuwa ni mazao yanayokomaa baadaye.
sw.R: Lakini ngano haikuharibika. Wala aina nyingine ya ngano iitwayo spelti haikuharibika. Hiyo huota baadaye katika mwaka.

decisions.choice: spelt: a hardy kind of wheat
decisions.reason: The word names a coarse wheat grown in Egypt and Israel (Isaiah 28:25; Ezekiel 4:9), probably emmer or spelt.

decisions.choice: late: late-ripening
decisions.reason: These grains were still young and low when the hail came, so they were not ruined. The locusts later eat what the hail left (10:5, 15).

decisions.choice: another kind of wheat called spelt
decisions.reason: Readable says what spelt is.

decisions.choice: "spelti" for the spelt
decisions.reason: Swahili has no everyday name for this hardy wheat (m1), so the name is borrowed, as English "spelt"; Readable explains it as "aina nyingine ya ngano", following the English Readable. "Mtama" is sorghum, a different grain.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה מֵעִ֤ם פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר וַיִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּפָּ֖יו אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחְדְּל֤וּ הַקֹּלוֹת֙ וְהַבָּרָ֔ד וּמָטָ֖ר לֹא־נִתַּ֥ךְ אָֽרְצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Moses from with Pharaoh [out of] the city, and spread out his palms to Yahweh, and ceased the thunders and the hail, and rain not was poured out to [the] earth.

en.L: And Moses went out from Pharaoh, out of the city, and spread out his palms to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and the thunder and the hail ceased, and rain was not poured out upon the earth.
en.B: So Moses left Pharaoh and went outside the city, where he spread his hands out toward {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The thunder and hail came to an end, and the rain stopped pouring onto the ground.
en.R: Moses left Pharaoh and went outside the city. He raised his hands to pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the thunder and hail stopped, and no more rain fell.

es.L: Y salió Moisés de [junto al] faraón, fuera de la ciudad, y extendió sus palmas {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}; y cesaron los truenos y el granizo, y la lluvia no se derramó sobre la tierra.
es.B: Moisés, pues, dejó al faraón y salió de la ciudad, y allí extendió las manos hacia {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Los truenos y el granizo terminaron, y la lluvia dejó de caer a cántaros sobre el suelo.
es.R: Moisés se fue de donde estaba el faraón y salió de la ciudad. Levantó las manos para orar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Entonces se acabaron los truenos y el granizo, y no cayó más lluvia.

fr.L: Et Moïse sortit de chez Pharaon, hors de la ville, et étendit ses paumes vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; et les tonnerres et la grêle cessèrent, et la pluie ne se déversa plus sur la terre.
fr.B: Moïse quitta donc Pharaon et sortit de la ville ; là, il tendit les mains vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Le tonnerre et la grêle prirent fin, et la pluie cessa de tomber à verse sur le sol.
fr.R: Moïse a quitté Pharaon et il est sorti de la ville. Il a levé les mains pour prier {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Alors le tonnerre et la grêle se sont arrêtés, et il n’est plus tombé de pluie.

sw.L: Naye Musa akatoka kwa Farao, nje ya mji, akavikunjua viganja vyake kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; na ngurumo na mvua ya mawe zikakoma, wala mvua haikumwagika juu ya nchi.
sw.B: Basi Musa aliondoka kwa Farao, akatoka nje ya mji, akanyoosha mikono yake kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ngurumo na mvua ya mawe zikakoma, na mvua ikaacha kumwagika ardhini.
sw.R: Musa aliondoka kwa Farao, akatoka nje ya mji. Akainua mikono yake kumwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ndipo ngurumo na mvua ya mawe zikakoma, wala mvua haikunyesha tena.

decisions.choice: rain was not poured out: the downpour stopped
decisions.reason: Rain is mentioned here for the first time; the storm brought rain as well as hail. The verb is used of pouring out liquid or molten metal.

decisions.choice: spread out his palms: Moses did as he had said
decisions.reason: He keeps the word of verse 29, and the storm ends as he said it would.

decisions.choice: raised his hands to pray
decisions.reason: As in verse 29, Readable says that the gesture is prayer.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא פַּרְעֹ֗ה כִּֽי־חָדַ֨ל הַמָּטָ֧ר וְהַבָּרָ֛ד וְהַקֹּלֹ֖ת וַיֹּ֣סֶף לַחֲטֹ֑א וַיַּכְבֵּ֥ד לִבּ֖וֹ ה֥וּא וַעֲבָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Pharaoh that had ceased the rain and the hail and the thunders, and he continued to sin, and made heavy his heart, he and his servants.

en.L: And Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunder had ceased, and he sinned again, and he made his heart heavy, he and his servants.
en.B: Once Pharaoh saw that rain, hail, and thunder had all ceased, he went back to sinning: he hardened his heart, and so did his officials.
en.R: Pharaoh saw that the rain, hail, and thunder had stopped. Then he sinned once more. He made himself stubborn, and his officials did too.

es.L: Y vio el faraón que habían cesado la lluvia, el granizo y los truenos, y volvió a pecar, e hizo pesado su corazón, él y sus siervos.
es.B: En cuanto el faraón vio que la lluvia, el granizo y los truenos habían cesado, volvió a pecar: endureció su corazón, y lo mismo hicieron sus funcionarios.
es.R: El faraón vio que la lluvia, el granizo y los truenos se habían detenido. Entonces pecó otra vez. Se puso terco, y sus funcionarios también.

fr.L: Et Pharaon vit que la pluie, la grêle et les tonnerres avaient cessé, et il pécha de nouveau, et il appesantit son cœur, lui et ses serviteurs.
fr.B: Dès que Pharaon vit que la pluie, la grêle et le tonnerre avaient cessé, il se remit à pécher : il endurcit son cœur, et ses officiers firent de même.
fr.R: Pharaon a vu que la pluie, la grêle et le tonnerre s’étaient arrêtés. Alors il a de nouveau péché. Il est devenu têtu, et ses officiers aussi.

sw.L: Naye Farao alipoona kwamba mvua na mvua ya mawe na ngurumo zimekoma, akaendelea kutenda dhambi, akaufanya mzito moyo wake, yeye na watumishi wake.
sw.B: Farao alipoona kwamba mvua, mvua ya mawe na ngurumo zimekoma, alirudia kutenda dhambi: akaufanya moyo wake kuwa mgumu, yeye pamoja na maafisa wake.
sw.R: Farao aliona kwamba mvua, mvua ya mawe na ngurumo zimekoma. Ndipo akatenda dhambi tena. Akawa mkaidi, na maafisa wake vilevile.

decisions.choice: he sinned again: Pharaoh goes back on his confession
decisions.reason: Pharaoh said "I have sinned" in verse 27. Breaking his promise is itself sin, as Moses had warned (8:25; 9:30).

decisions.choice: made his heart heavy, he and his servants: the court joins Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The verb from the root "heavy" (see 7:3, 14). For the first time Pharaoh's officials are said to share his hard heart; in 10:1 God says he has made both heavy.

decisions.choice: hardened his heart / made himself stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "made his heart heavy"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: his officials
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are his court and officials (5:21; 8:5). Balanced and Readable say "officials"; Literal keeps "servants".

source.text: וַֽיֶּחֱזַק֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And was strong [the] heart of Pharaoh, and not he let go the sons of Israel, just as had said Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses.

en.L: And the heart of Pharaoh was strong, and he did not let the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel go, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said by the hand of Moses.
en.B: Pharaoh remained stubborn and refused to release the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. It was as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had foretold through Moses.
en.R: Pharaoh stayed stubborn. He would not let the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} go. This was just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke through Moses.

es.L: Y el corazón del faraón se hizo fuerte, y no dejó ir a los hijos de Israel, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho por mano de Moisés.
es.B: El faraón siguió obstinado y se negó a dejar salir a los israelitas. Fue tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había anunciado por medio de Moisés.
es.R: El faraón siguió terco. No quiso dejar ir a los israelitas. Esto era justo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho que pasaría cuando habló por medio de Moisés.

fr.L: Et le cœur de Pharaon fut fort, et il ne laissa pas aller les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait dit par la main de Moïse.
fr.B: Pharaon resta obstiné et refusa de laisser partir les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Il en fut comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait annoncé par Moïse.
fr.R: Pharaon est resté têtu. Il n’a pas voulu laisser partir les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. C’était exactement ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait annoncé quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait parlé par Moïse.

sw.L: Na moyo wa Farao ukawa imara, wala hakuwaacha wana wa Israeli waende, kama vile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amesema kwa mkono wa Musa.
sw.B: Farao aliendelea kuwa mkaidi, akakataa kuwaachilia Waisraeli. Ikawa kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa ametabiri kupitia Musa.
sw.R: Farao alibaki mkaidi. Hakutaka kuwaacha Waisraeli waende. Hili ndilo jambo ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amesema lingetokea alipozungumza kupitia Musa.

decisions.choice: the heart was strong: Pharaoh's will stayed set
decisions.reason: The verb "be strong", as in 7:13, 22 and 8:15; see the note at 7:3. The plague ends as the earlier ones did.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: God's word came to Pharaoh through Moses as his spokesman (4:21; 7:2-4).

decisions.choice: remained stubborn / stayed stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "was strong"; Balanced and Readable say what a strong heart means here.
